text.slice: Automated Porting of ColorOS / OxygenOS / RealmeUI

This guide describes the process of creating a port using the auto-port script. The port is built on the basis of two firmware packages: the base (ColorOS/OxygenOS/RealmeUI — the donor shell) and the stock firmware of the phone to which the port is being transferred.
Important rule: Any base with the same processor (SoC) as the target device is suitable for porting — MTK only to MTK, Qualcomm only to Qualcomm.
Step 1. Preparing and Unpacking Firmware
Unpack the payload.bin files of both firmware packages. For the automatic script to work correctly, the folders must be named strictly in a certain way:
Name the stock firmware project "stok" MANDATORILY
Name the base (donor) firmware project "port" MANDATORILY
From the base firmware (into the port folder), extract the following partitions:
system, system_ext, product, all my_** (my_manifest, my_product, etc.), vendor, odm
From the stock firmware (into the stok folder), extract the following partitions:
vendor, odm, system_ext, **_dlkm (if present)
Step 2. Merging my-partitions with system
Run the special my partition merge script.
Step 3. Running the Auto-port Script
After the merge is complete, run the main auto-port script.
Step 4. Proper Building
After the script has successfully completed, you can proceed to repacking the images.
It is recommended to build images in erofs, raw format.
Build the following partitions from the base folder (port):
system, product, system_ext
Build the following partitions from the stock folder (stok):
vendor, odm, all **_dlkm (including system_dlkm)
The vendor partition from any Android version is suitable for the port — to any Android version of the base.
Step 5. Troubleshooting First Boot (Bootloop)
If the device does not boot after building and flashing (bootloop):
Try forcibly replacing all VNDK APEX files in the port/system_ext/apex/ folder with versions from the stok folder.
After these actions, the firmware should boot.
If the device still does not boot — try changing the base (remember about matching SoC processors, see the first step).
